summary: Transparent midstream proxy insertion causing serialized streaming and long tail latency between APAC and EU
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 03:20 UTC StreamlineAI sees high p95/p99 latency and streaming timeouts for inference requests originating in APAC and routed to eu-west. Symptoms point to an intermediate transparent proxy that is serializing HTTP/2 streams and introducing head-of-line delays; streaming responses are returned in full chunks rather than interleaved tokens, causing user-observed stalls and occasional 504s at the application layer. Impact: customer-facing production service degradation, active customer requests timing out or experiencing multi-second tail latency, increased error rates in their monitoring. Environment: production, apac-east region for client egress, destination region eu-west hosting model endpoints.

Expected behavior: streaming responses should arrive token-by-token (low TTFB, steady token stream). Observed behavior: initial handshake fine, then long pauses between token batches; tcpdump/traces show additional hop and increased TLS handshake + connect times.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From an APAC client sim (or from apac-east runbook host) send a streaming /v1/generate request pinned to eu-west using account token for StreamlineAI.
2) Observe the stream: instead of token-by-token frames, tokens arrive in large batches separated by multi-second gaps; p99 token latency > 5s.
3) Capture packet trace (tcpdump -w) and run H2 frame inspect; note single connection with serialized DATA frames and delayed ACKs.
4) Run traceroute and tcptraceroute to eu-west model endpoint and compare AS path to previous baseline; note extra hop through peer AS reported below.
logs: edge-proxy: connect_time_ms spike from median 18ms -> 420ms for flows to eu-west (03:20 UTC)
serving-runtime: stream_chunk_dispatch delayed: queue_depth on egress-socket increased to 128 (03:21-03:40 UTC)
tcpdump: TLS handshake 1.2 resumed, but full handshake round trips increased by +3 (SYN->ACK->TLS) during spike window
app-logs: client-side 504 after 30s on 12% of streaming sessions (customer telemetry)
investigation_notes: 03:30 UTC - Support initial triage: confirmed customer-reported symptoms and requested packet captures and traceroutes.
03:45 UTC - SRE found AS path for several affected flows now transits through peer AS 64521 which is not in our baseline (baseline was direct transit).
04:10 UTC - Observed intermediate device rewriting TLS session parameters causing session-resume fallbacks and additional RTTs; proxy appears to be a transparent TCP/SSL proxy at upstream peering.
04:40 UTC - Proxy does not preserve HTTP/2 stream multiplexing; it queues/subdivides frames resulting in coarse-grained delivery (token batching) which explains serialized streaming behavior.
05:00 UTC - Workaround validated: forcing route to a different peering (edge-egress-policy override) restored streaming-token granularity and reduced p99 latency to baseline for customers tested.

Hypothesis: recent BGP/peering announcement at provider edge caused path shift through third-party transparent proxy/inspection appliance in APAC transit. That device does not support HTTP/2 streaming properly and is intentionally buffering/aggregating frames for inspection.

resolution: Workaround: applied edge-egress override to prefer alternate peering for affected account (temporary). Root cause: provider-side peering change routed traffic through a transparent inspection proxy that buffers HTTP/2 frames causing streaming serialization. Next steps: Network to negotiate peer fix or avoid peer via permanent routing policy; Product to add detection for serialized streaming anomalies. Customer notified and monitoring continues.
